paras: The Excelsior Springs jail whipping took place on the night of August 27, 1895, when men took two prisoners, one Black and one white, from the city jail at Excelsior Springs, Missouri, and whipped them. Both men were then released, and wire reports headlined the attack as the work of "whitecaps" and said the town's Black residents were pressing for a legal investigation.

The two prisoners, who were not named, were held in the Excelsior Springs city jail. The Kansas City Daily Journal said they "had confessed to a nameless crime," while a wire item dated August 29 said they were "charged with viciousness"; neither report named the offense.

According to a special dispatch to the Kansas City Daily Journal dated August 28, "someone" went to the jail the night before and took out "a colored man and a white man." The two were taken about a mile from the city, where the Black man was stripped and severely whipped. In the Journal's version the white man "begged off," and both were then allowed to go free.
The briefer August 29 wire item described the attackers as "masked men" and the prisoners as "a negro and an Irishman," and said both were whipped with cowhides.

A dispatch dated August 31 reported that nothing had been heard from the two men since they were whipped "Tuesday night." It added that "the colored people are highly incensed and have taken steps to have it legally investigated." No report of arrests, an investigation's result or a prosecution appears in the coverage.

The whipping reached readers only as short telegraphic items in white papers in Missouri, Kansas and Nebraska. The Kansas City Daily Journal printed it first, on August 29, among its "Telegraphic Briefs," with the fullest detail and no comment. The Leavenworth Herald of August 31 ran the wire version under the headline "Whipped by Whitecaps," between items on grasshoppers and a body found near South McAlester.

The follow-up appeared under "White Caps to be Prosecuted" in The Frontier of O'Neill, Nebraska, on September 5 and in The McCook Tribune on September 6, in identical wire columns. That headline went further than its text, which reported only that Black residents were seeking an investigation. No coverage of the whipping was found in the Black press.

The two accounts differ on whether the white prisoner was whipped: the Kansas City Daily Journal said he "begged off" and only the Black man was whipped, while the August 29 wire item said both were whipped with cowhides. The Journal's report was earlier and more detailed, and came from a paper near Excelsior Springs.

accounts.label: Wire report (Aug. 29)

framing.detail: The Kansas City Daily Journal ran the item among its 'Telegraphic Briefs' without comment, calling the charge only 'a nameless crime.'
The Leavenworth Herald ran the Aug. 29 wire item under 'Whipped by Whitecaps' among other one-paragraph dispatches.
Two Nebraska weeklies ran the Aug. 31 follow-up under 'White Caps to be Prosecuted,' reporting the Black residents' anger and push for an investigation.
